audit_findings.title: The DCF extends current WAKIX economics through a known 2030 generic entry
audit_findings.magnitude: reported terminal-value share is 47.7%-51.5%; post-generic erosion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The generic entry falls within the explicit forecast and affects future owner earnings, growth, and the terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Under the terms of the settlement agreement, the litigation between the parties in the United States District Court for the District of Delaware will be dismissed, and Hikma will have a license to sell its generic product beginning March 2030 if WAKIX receives pediatric exclusivity, or earlier under certain circumstances.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated model-perimeter error, not merely a possible future risk. Licensed generic entry can begin in March 2030, while the valuation applies smooth growth followed by 2.5% perpetual growth without an explicit WAKIX erosion step. Because roughly half of reported value comes from the terminal value and all current revenue is from WAKIX, the omission is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rerun every scenario with explicit WAKIX price, volume, margin, and royalty erosion beginning no later than March 2030; include replacement products only through separately probability-adjusted cash flows.

audit_findings.title: Pipeline replacement cash flows carry substantial unmodeled contingent consideration
audit_findings.magnitude: $645.0 million maximum Epygenix consideration ($130.0 million development/regulatory plus $515.0 million sales-based), equal to $9.49 per diluted share or 21.5% of base equity value; probability-weighted amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Success-triggered milestones reduce owner earnings or the equity bridge associated with pipeline cash flows used to replace WAKIX after generic entry.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, the Company will be obligated to pay up to $ 130,000 upon the achievement of development and regulatory milestones and up to $ 515,000 upon the achievement of certain sales-based milestones, in each case to Epygenix’s former stockholders.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual payments are demonstrated, although they are contingent rather than present liabilities. Their maximum scale is material relative to the $3.006 billion base equity value. Because post-2030 growth requires replacement economics, any pipeline value credited without its matched milestone, royalty, and option costs can overstate common-equity value.
audit_findings.action: Inventory all unpaid Epygenix, Bioprojet, ConSynance, CiRC, CVR, Novitium, and MSN obligations; probability-weight and time each payment consistently with the product cash flow that triggers it, then rerun the DCF.

audit_findings.title: Unpaid patent settlements may remain outside the latest cash bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: June 30, 2026 legal and professional fee accrual was $4.978 million, equal to $0.07 per diluted share and 0.17% of base equity value; settlement component unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unpaid non-operating settlement should reduce the excess-cash bridge because its expense was already reflected in historical owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Unpaid settlements as of December 31, 2025, have been recognized in accrued expenses on the Company’s consolidated balance sheets as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated bridge error: the latest filing does not identify a remaining settlement balance. Even conservatively treating the entire $4.978 million legal and professional accrual as an omitted settlement would reduce value by only about $0.07 per share and would not change any scenario's relationship to the $42.25 market price.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 30 accrued-liability ledger and subsequent-payment detail; deduct only the settlement amount still unpaid and avoid deducting recurring legal fees.

audit_findings.title: Cash-like long-term investments may have been omitted after their income was purged
audit_findings.magnitude: $294.668 million, equal to $4.33 per diluted share and 9.8% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The omitted marketable debt securities belong in the equity bridge because their interest income was purged from owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: The investments classified as noncurrent have original maturity dates ranging from 1 - 2 years .
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated bridge error. The reported $667.791 million equals June 30 cash of $549.769 million plus short-term investments of $118.022 million and therefore excludes the separately filed $294.668 million of long-term investments. Adding those securities would raise the bear value from $38.94 to approximately $43.27 per share, reversing its comparison with the $42.25 market price.
audit_findings.action: Add the $294.668 million June 30 fair value of long-term investments to the bridge, confirm none is restricted or operationally committed, and rerun all per-share values and margin-of-safety thresholds.

audit_findings.title: The latest-actual anchor contains unusually large patent-litigation and settlement costs
audit_findings.magnitude: $39.0 million pre-tax expense increase, equal to 23.4% of the $166.4 million owner-earnings anchor; sustainable normalization amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A discrete expense embedded in the latest-actual anchor depresses owner earnings and is then capitalized through every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase was primarily due to a $39.0 million increase in legal and professional fees, primarily associated with patent lawsuits and settlements, a $1.1 million increase in personnel costs associated with a higher headcount and a $2.1 million increase associated with travel and conference attendance.
audit_findings.explanation: The $39.0 million increase is demonstrated, but the record does not separate recurring patent-defense costs from settlement amounts or establish a dollar-for-dollar owner-earnings adjustment. Its scale relative to the anchor makes the normalization question material. The 2026 filing's lower legal and professional expense supports reviewing recurrence but does not by itself establish the correct normalized amount.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $39.0 million increase to individual settlement, litigation, and recurring legal invoices; normalize only demonstrably nonrecurring expense, retain recurring defense costs, and separately deduct any unpaid settlement in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: A deferred-tax remeasurement was retained in the anchor year
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $7.53 million computed from 3.5% of $215.064 million pretax income, equal to 4.5% of anchor owner earnings; computed DCF sensitivity is approximately $1.32-$1.84 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The one-period deferred-tax remeasurement reduces the owner-earnings anchor and therefore forecast owner earnings and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in our effective tax rate for the year ended December 31, 2025, was primarily driven by the remeasurement of state deferred tax assets that was incurred during the year ended December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a 3.5-percentage-point 2025 tax-rate effect, although the exact ledger charge and its treatment in the owner-earnings calculation should be verified. Even a full dollar-for-dollar $7.53 million add-back would leave the bear value below the $42.25 price, leave the base and bull values above it, and remain far short of closing the $11.30 gap between price and the $30.95 buy-below threshold.
audit_findings.action: Verify the exact deferred-tax remeasurement and whether the owner-earnings construction already reversed it; if retained, rerun with the one-time charge removed and a separately supported recurring cash-tax rate.
